Okay, so I'm trying to figure out how many more blocks (layers) are in the BERT base encoder compared to the encoder from the architecture proposed in "Attention is All You Need." I remember that BERT is a model developed by Google, and it's based on the Transformer architecture. 

First, I think about what I know about BERT. I recall that BERT-base has 12 layers. That's a common fact, so I'm pretty confident about that. Now, the other part is the original Transformer encoder from the "Attention is All You Need" paper. I believe that model has 8 layers. 

So, if BERT has 12 layers and the original has 8, subtracting the two gives 4 more layers in BERT. That makes sense because BERT adds more layers to the encoder to capture more context, which helps with understanding the text better.

Wait, but I'm not entirely sure if I'm remembering the layer counts correctly. Maybe I should double-check. I think the original Transformer has 6 attention heads but 8 layers. BERT, on the other hand, uses the same attention mechanism but increases the number of layers to 12. So yes, that's a difference of 4 layers.

I don't see any mistakes in this reasoning. Both models are well-documented, so the layer counts should be accurate. Therefore, the conclusion is correct.
</think>
